programme: No shared module is nameable from these factors. They span unrelated regulatory identities — GATA3 (Th2 cytokine/epidermal differentiation regulator), SF1 (steroidogenic nuclear receptor driving CYP11A1/HSD3B2/STAR), JARID2 (PRC2 Polycomb subunit), MTA1 (NuRD chromatin-remodeling/metastasis factor), CIC (RAS-MAPK transcriptional repressor), BCLAF1 (splicing/apoptosis factor), TBPL1 (testis-lineage TBP paralog), HMGB2 (chromatin architectural protein), SP2 (Sp-family promoter-proximal factor), ELK3 (ETS/MAPK-responsive factor), CREBZF (lipid/energy metabolism regulator), and HOXA5 (developmental homeobox factor). Their target lists barely overlap, and where they do (TP53, CDKN1A, TH) it is through generic stress-response or apoptosis hub genes that sit downstream of dozens of unrelated pathways, not a specific complex or pathway these factors build together.
role_in_a: Only GATA3 has any disease-linked evidence in Alzheimer's Disease, and it is indirect (a pleiotropy scan linking it to blood pressure/cognitive traits, PMID 40951946), not a mechanistic role. None of the other ten factors have papers that establish an Alzheimer's role from the material retrieved.
role_in_b: Only GATA3 has direct evidence in psoriasis: it is reported decreased in psoriatic epidermis and induced by narrow-band UVB treatment (PMID 21611195), consistent with its known role in keratinocyte differentiation and Th2 balance. None of the other ten factors have psoriasis literature at all.
shared_axis: No mechanism connects these two tissues through this factor set. GATA3 individually has a plausible but disease-specific role in each condition (systemic blood-pressure/cognition association in AD; local epidermal/Th2 regulation in psoriasis), but those are not the same axis, and the other eleven factors provide no bridge between them.
reasoning: Twelve factors recurring across patient groups is a statistical pattern, not evidence of a shared programme: their target sets and known biology (steroidogenesis, Polycomb repression, NuRD remodeling, RAS-MAPK repression, splicing, lipid metabolism, developmental patterning) point in mutually unrelated directions. Literature support is essentially confined to GATA3, and even that is one paper per disease in non-overlapping contexts, so there is neither a nameable module nor a documented or inferable shared axis to report.
support: PMID 40951946 — genome-wide pleiotropy analysis linking GATA3 locus to blood pressure and cognitive performance, not a mechanistic AD study; PMID 21611195 — GATA3 expression decreased in psoriatic skin and induced by narrow-band UVB, direct evidence of a psoriasis role; PMID 25937287 and PMID 28669840 — implicate HMGB2 in chromatin-associated regulation of LRP1 antisense transcript and in a senescence-accelerated mouse brain circRNA network respectively, suggestive of AD-adjacent biology but not disease-establishing and with no psoriasis counterpart; all other retrieved papers for SF1, HOXA5, MTA1, JARID2, CIC, BCLAF1, TBPL1, SP2, ELK3, CREBZF are off-topic (wrong entity, wrong disease, or unclear) per the reader's notes.
how_to_falsify: Run a STRING/BioGRID protein-interaction and co-expression analysis across all twelve factors in matched Alzheimer's brain and psoriasis skin transcriptomic datasets; if they cluster into a shared complex, shared upstream regulator, or co-regulated module rather than behaving as independent, pathway-unrelated regulators, that would overturn the incoherent call. Conversely, targeted ChIP-seq for GATA3 in AD-relevant brain cell types (microglia/neurons) testing for binding at the pleiotropy-implicated loci from PMID 40951946 would clarify whether GATA3's AD association is mechanistic rather than incidental to blood pressure.
caveats: 64 patient-group comparisons drawn from only 6 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance counts are not fully independent replications. Brain and skin share no direct anatomical or clinical relationship, raising the bar for any claimed shared axis. The tissue-generic exclusion list (NR3C1, TAL1, RFX5, EGR4, NOTCH1, STAT4, ZEB1, SOX10, HDAC7) shows that generic immune/tissue regulators were already stripped out before ranking, so the remaining factors are genuinely pair-specific — but pair-specific recurrence did not translate into any identifiable shared mechanism, which is itself the informative result here.
